discovery: Proposal and experimental realization of quantum logic and quantum computation with trapped ions

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Rainer Blatt
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Quantum information science / atomic and quantum optics
motivation: In 1995 Cirac and Zoller showed how a string of laser-cooled ions, coupled through their shared motion, could implement a universal set of quantum gates. This was the first concrete, scalable architecture for a quantum computer, and it set the template that every later platform, superconducting circuits included, has followed: addressable qubits, a quantum bus and high-fidelity entangling gates. Blatt turned the blueprint into reality. His group realized the Cirac-Zoller gate, deterministic teleportation, multi-qubit entangled states, quantum error correction and programmable quantum simulation, routinely achieving fidelities that define the state of the art. Together, their work is a rare example of theory and experiment advancing hand in hand. It opened a new regime of controllable many-body quantum physics and founded the field of practical quantum information processing. The 2012 prize recognized measurement of individual quantum systems; this nomination recognizes using them to compute.
